sentences.text:
Smt. Manisha Shukla, Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St
 Order

This is second application under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 has been filed on behalf of the applicant namely Sukhlal for grant of regular bail, who is behind the bars since 15.09.2024 in connection with Crime No.262/2024 registered at Police Station Mandhata District Khandwa, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(3), 376(2)(j), 506 of IPC and Sections 4,
5(j) (ii), 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Applicant's first bail application (M.Cr.C.No.7234/2025) was dismissed as got withdrawn on 22.03.2025 with liberty to file anew after recording of the statement of prosecutrix and her parents.
Since, such statements have been recorded, the applicant has renewed his prayer for bail availing previous liberty.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant sanguinely submits that the applicant is innocent and has been fallaciously roped in the crime.

He further submits that at the initial stage of investigation and in the statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, the prosecutrix has stated against unknown person whereas she was well- acquainted with the applicant and therefore there was no reason for not disclosing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9200 2 MCRC-57673-2025 his name earlier.
He also submits that as per the prosecution portrayal, the prosecutrix became pregnant but DNA qua the applicant negates his association.
He also submits that the applicant is in incarceration since 15.09.2024 and the trial will take its usual course to conclude.
On these premise, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be granted bail.

4. In contrast, learned counsel for the respondent/State pinpointing the adolescence of prosecutrix submits that she was only 14 years of age at the time of incident and therefore looking to the nature of offence, no case of bail is made out.
Thus, she prays for dismissal of the application.

It is directed that the applicant namely Sukhlal be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by it in this regard during the pendency of trial.
6. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 480(3) of BNSS.
